title: SafeWindow replay veneer for analytics: hybrid stream-batch rewriter with tenant-aware cost caps
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a reusable replay veneer (SafeWindow) that can safely run hybrid stream/batch replays for console usage analytics. The veneer should apply schema-aware transforms, enforce tenant-level cost and throughput caps, and produce auditable, idempotent output suitable for downstream metric recomputation and billing. This ticket covers the orchestration layer, checkpoint format, and safety controls; a follow-up will plug into the heavy-weight rewriter for data transformations.
background: We frequently run ad-hoc and scheduled backfills to recompute derived metrics after schema changes or bug fixes. Existing replays either lack tenant-level throttles (causing noisy production impact) or don't expose a dry-run validation with full hashing-based equivalence checks. SafeWindow introduces a time-windowed execution model + tenant caps to allow safe, multi-tenant backfills without destabilizing online systems.
goals: Provide a SafeWindow abstraction: execute replay work in overlapping, restartable windows with deterministic checkpoints
Implement tenant-aware rate and spend caps to prevent any single tenant from exceeding a configured budget during the backfill
Support schema-aware transform hooks and a dry-run validation path that computes output diffs without committing to downstream stores
Emit tracing and audit artifacts per-window and per-tenant for post-mortem and billing reconciliation
Provide a canary mode (subset of tenants + day-range) and automatic rollback on regression thresholds
non_goals: Do not implement new heavy-weight transformation logic here (that belongs in the rewriter library)
Not responsible for long-term archival of historical raw events
design_notes: SafeWindow uses watermarking derived from event timestamps and a lightweight lease-per-window model. Each window writes a checkpoint object containing (window_id, tenant_id, last_processed_offset, output_hash_snapshot, cost_consumed). Checkpoints are stored in the console control-plane bucket (encrypted). We will leverage the existing streaming consumer to feed 'live' events into the same transform path used by the batch rewriter to maximize code reuse. Tenant caps are enforced via a token bucket that draws from a configured budget (tokens proportional to estimated output cost). The architecture supports a dry-run flow that calculates output diffs and writes a signed validation report to the audit store without applying changes.
implementation_plan: Spec: finalize checkpoint schema and cost-token model (PRD link)
Platform: add checkpoint storage and housekeeping worker (control-plane S3 + lifecycle)
Orchestration: implement window lease allocator and restart logic
Safety: implement tenant token bucket service and per-window observability
Validation: build a dry-run validator that computes output hashes and diff reports
Ops: add console endpoints to start/abort backfills, and a dashboard for live window metrics
QA: smoke tests with synthetic tenants, canary run on staging, regression thresholds
acceptance_criteria: SafeWindow can run a 7-day historical replay across 100 tenants without exceeding configured per-tenant spend limits in staging
Dry-run validation produces a signed report with output hash per-window and flags any diffs above configured thresholds
Checkpointing supports resume-after-failure semantics with idempotent reprocessing of window segments
Operational dashboard surfaces per-window latency, tokens consumed, and top failing transforms
Runbook for abort/rollback tested and documented
progress_updates: 2025-01-17: Kickoff meeting with analytics, platform, and infra; agreed on checkpoint fields and encryption requirements (Confluence: /docs/safewindow-spec)
2025-01-24: Prototype of checkpoint writer + lease allocator merged to feature branch (github.com/redwood/console-replay PR #312)
2025-01-30: Tenant token bucket service sketched; decided to reuse runtime cost-estimator module to compute token cost per output row
2025-02-05: Dry-run validator PoC produced diff reports for synthetic sample; identified edge-case with out-of-order timestamps requiring watermark smoothing
2025-02-10: Integration test in staging found a performance regression when running >50 concurrent windows; investigation in progress (profiling linked)
2025-02-12: Added temporary backpressure to orchestrator while we tune the batching heuristics; planning a staged canary for next week
risks: Underestimated cost model leading to token budget overruns unless conservative defaults are used
Checkpoint format changes become a migration burden; we will version checkpoints explicitly
Large tenants with very high event density could still saturate downstream stores despite token caps if transforms expand payloads
Latency-sensitive live consumers might be impacted if shared resources are not properly isolated
mitigations: Start with conservative token budgets and monitor a basket of tenants in staging
Versioned checkpoint schema with a migration shim that supports both v1 and v2 during rollout
Offer optional tenant isolation (run on dedicated worker pool) for the 1% of tenants that elect it
Implement per-window priority weighting and backpressure when downstream traces exceed thresholds
decisions: Use S3 encrypted control-plane bucket for checkpoint storage (server-side encryption with KMS)
Dry-run mode writes signed reports to the audit store and does not touch downstream metric stores
Token bucket cost estimation will reuse existing runtime cost-estimator; we will add a conservative multiplier for batch runs
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus on checkpoint format and the tenant token model. The current PoC uses a best-effort cost multiplier; we need feedback from billing on accuracy and acceptable conservative factors. Also confirm KMS configuration for control-plane bucket before merge.
